provenance.instrument: Kennett Square Borough Code Chapter 23 Zoning, as published on Municode (Supplement 30)
provenance.status_detail: Municode: 'Supplement 30. Online content updated on September 26, 2025.' 'Codified through ... Ord. 985, passed August 4, 2025.' Adopted ordinances not yet codified: Ord. No. 987 and 986 (11/5/25, tax rates and police pension). The ADU text in 23-30 carries history through 'Ord. No. 983, §§ 2, 3, 8-4-2025'. The Zoneomics copy linked in the index has the same text and was used to read the whole chapter. Key passages were checked on Municode. Rechecked 2026-11-26: news reports (Inquirer 2026-08-18) confirm Council adopted the short-term rental cap ordinance on 2026-08-17 (about 20 units, existing ones grandfathered). Its text was not found online, so its effect on Table 17 and 23-30 is still not read.
provenance.code_current_through_note: Municode on 2026-11-13: Supplement 30, online September 26, 2025, codified through Ord. 985 passed August 4, 2025.
provenance.code_caution: The online code is current only to August 4, 2025. Borough Council passed a short-term rental ordinance on or about August 17, 2026 (news reports, text and number not seen). As reported it caps short-term rentals at 20 in the Borough, bars a single-family house as a short-term rental, and limits future short-term rentals to accessory units such as garages or guest houses, owner occupied during the stay. It likely amends Table 17 and may amend 23-30. A proposed 2026 amendment (single-family stacked dwellings in R-3, multifamily in OI-2, Chester County review ZA-01-26-18774) was not seen either. Also, 23-30(c)(2)(B)(vii) says 'The following standards are required for detached ADUs;' for lots on alleys, but no list follows. Ask the Borough for the current text.
checks: Two kinds of unit, both accessory uses by right to a residential use: an 'accessory apartment' inside the house, and an 'accessory dwelling unit' in an accessory building on a lot with a detached single-family house (23-7, 23-30(a)(4)(A))

Accessory apartment: at most 50% of the square footage of the house, in the upper floors, basement, rear of the house, or a carriage house or garage, with its own kitchen, bath and either its own outside door or a common hall or balcony (23-30(c)(1))

Accessory dwelling unit: at most 1,000 sq ft of living space (interior rooms) and two bedrooms. One per parcel. It may not be subdivided off and stays in single ownership (23-30(c)(2)(B)(v), (vi), (viii))
Detached ADU height: the lesser of 25 ft or the height of the house. An existing structure over 25 ft keeps its own height (23-30(c)(2)(B)(i))

Detached ADU in the rear yard only (not a front or side yard), at least 6 ft from the side and rear lot lines. The rear setback does not apply where the rear backs up to an alley, but the code gives no alley figure (23-30(c)(2)(B), (ii), (iii))

The definition puts an accessory apartment 'within the principal dwelling unit', but 23-30(c)(1)(B) also allows it 'in a carriage house or garage'. On a twin or townhouse lot, where an ADU in an accessory building is not allowed, ask whether an accessory apartment in a garage is (23-7, 23-30(c)(1)(B))

Short-term rentals: a 2026 ordinance (passed about August 17, 2026, not read) reportedly limits future short-term rentals to accessory units, owner occupied, at most 20 in the Borough. Ask the Borough
Lots under 15,000 sq ft may have two accessory structures in all, a detached garage included. Only one may be an ADU (23-30(c)(2)(B)(iv))
Lots on alleys: the code says standards are required for detached ADUs along alleys, but lists none. A scaled engineered or architectural plan goes with the building permit (23-30(c)(2)(B)(vii))
Parking: 1 space per bedroom, at most 2, for an accessory apartment or ADU, plus 2 for the house (23-65 Table 7.1)
No owner-occupancy rule and no relative rule in 23-30
District lot tables give lot area 'per dwelling unit for residential uses'. Whether an ADU needs a second share of lot area is not settled (Tables 1, 3, 6, 8)
Short-term rentals are an allowable accessory use in every district listed in Table 17, subject to Borough Code chapter 8, article VII (not read) (23-28)
In the Historic District a change of use goes to Borough staff and may need a certificate of appropriateness from Borough Council (23-12(b), chapter 25)
Residential conversions of a house to more units are listed as special exceptions in R-3 and R-3/PAO, but 23-29(c)(11) says conditional use. Ask which applies
R-3 and R-3/PAO allow two-family detached and semi-detached dwellings by right on 2,000 sq ft per unit (23-15, 23-16)

C-2 allows by right 'Any use allowed as a by right use in the R-3 Zoning District' (23-19(b)(10)). Accessory uses for residential uses listed in 23-30 take the R-3 yards (23-19(e)(3)), and Table 12 gives residential uses the R-3 requirements
If the Borough treats a detached unit as a second principal dwelling, two principal buildings need twice the side yard and land development approval (23-32(b))
Parking may be reduced by special exception (23-65(b))
Only one principal use per lot unless approved as a conditional use (23-31)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Kennett Square Borough. Read on Municode in a browser and in the Zoneomics copy (same Supplement 30 text). Searched for accessory dwelling, accessory apartment, accessory habitation, alley, short-term rental, residential conversion. The index note on parking (1 space per bedroom, max 2) and the 25 ft and 6 ft figures agree with the code. Chester County Planning Commission material in the drive has no Kennett Square Borough entry. District codes: R-1, R-2, R-3, R-3/PAO, C-1, C-2, C-3, OI-1, OI-2, with FP, SS, MSD, RUA and TBO overlays.

term.note: 'Accessory dwelling unit' means a residential living unit on the same parcel as a detached single-family primary residential structure, in an accessory building and not located within the principal dwelling unit. A unit inside the house is an 'accessory apartment'.

status.note: 'An accessory use on the same lot and customarily incidental to a permitted principal use is permitted by right.' '(A) Accessory Habitation: (i) An accessory apartment as an accessory use. (ii) An accessory dwelling unit (limited to one per property).'

scope_districts.note: Table 17 marks 'Accessory Apartment' allowable in R-1, R-2a, R-3, R-3/PAO, C-1, C-2 and OI-1 (OI-1 only as accessory to a residential use). Table 17 has no ADU row. C-3 and OI-2 are not in Table 17.

status_outside.note: C-3 and OI-2 are not in Table 17.

path.note: Zoning and building permit. A detached ADU needs a scaled plan with the building permit (23-30(c)(2)(B)(vii)).

fallback_path.note: A unit that fails 23-30 needs a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board.

value.name: Two-family detached or semi-detached dwelling
value.conditions: 2,000 sq ft per unit in R-3 (3,500 in R-3/PAO), lot width 22 ft per unit, at least 5,000 sq ft per construction site, front 20, side 4 (14 total), rear 25, 35 ft.
value.note: A two-family building on its own lot. Building one in place of a house is a new principal use

value.name: Residential conversion of a house to more units
value.conditions: Lot area, yards, building area and parking of the district are not reduced. Utilities certified adequate. The resulting use must be permitted in the district. A converted house keeps one front entrance, parking in the rear yard, residential look, minimum floor areas of Borough ordinances. Historic structures follow the conditional use procedure and chapter 25.
value.note: The district lists and Table 16 say special exception. 23-29(c)(11)(A) says 'permitted in R-3 and R-3/PAO zoning districts by conditional use'

zoning_districts.note: Districts that permit a single-family detached dwelling by right and list the accessory apartment. C-2: 'Residential uses—Any use allowed as a by right use in the R-3 Zoning District' (23-19(b)(10)), and 'Accessory uses and structures for primarily residential land uses, as listed in section 23-30, will comply with the minimum yard requirements contained in subsection (g) of section 23-15' (23-19(e)(3)).

districts_in_doubt.note: Table 17 lists the accessory apartment here. C-1 permits only upper floor dwellings (23-18(b)(5)). OI-1 is marked 'As an accessory to a residential use only'.

existing_structure_only.note: A new accessory building may hold the ADU. An existing structure over 25 ft may be used at its own height.

requires_conforming_lot.note: 'A building may be constructed and expanded on a nonconforming, residential lot provided the minimum yard and maximum lot coverage requirements listed for the particular district are complied with.'

value.condition: A unit in an accessory building (an 'accessory dwelling unit') needs a detached single-family house on the parcel. On a twin or townhouse lot, ask whether an accessory apartment 'in a carriage house or garage' (23-30(c)(1)(B)) is allowed.
Lots under 15,000 sq ft may have no more than two accessory structures in all, a detached garage included. 15,000 to 29,000 sq ft: three. Only one may be an ADU.
A detached ADU along an alley should contribute to the character of the historic alleys. The code says standards are required but lists none. Ask the Borough.
An engineered or architectural plan, drawn to scale, goes with the building permit: the dwelling units, area and bulk criteria, stormwater, parking and exterior changes.

An accessory apartment is in the upper floors, basement, rear of the house, or a carriage house or garage, with its own kitchen, bath and either a separate outside door or a common hallway or balcony.
In the Historic District a change of use is reviewed by Borough staff and a certificate of appropriateness may be needed from Borough Council (chapter 25).
The ADU may not be subdivided from the principal parcel and stays in single ownership.

types_allowed.note: Accessory apartment: 'in the upper floors, basement, to the rear of the principal building, or in a carriage house or garage'. ADU: 'in an accessory building'. Reading: 'to the rear of the principal building' covers a rear addition.

value.attached: accessory apartment at the rear of the house

max_sqft.note: Caps differ by form. See below.

max_share_internal.note: Accessory apartment: 'not exceeding fifty percent of the square footage of the principal dwelling unit'.

max_sqft_accessory_building.note: 'An ADU shall be limited to a maximum of one thousand square feet of living space (defined as the square footage of the interior rooms therein) and no more than two bedrooms.' An accessory apartment placed in a carriage house or garage takes the 50% cap instead.

max_height_ft.note: 'The maximum building height for detached ADUs shall not exceed twenty-five feet or the height of the principal dwelling unit on the parcel, whichever is lesser.' An existing structure over 25 ft keeps its height.

setback_side_ft.note: 'Accessory dwelling units shall not be less than six feet from the side lot line.'

setback_rear_ft.note: 'not be less than six feet from the rear lot line unless the rear of the property backs up to an alley.'

setback_rear_alley_ft.note: The 6 ft rear setback does not apply on an alley, but no other figure is given.

front_yard_barred.note: 'Detached accessory structures may be erected within a rear yard'. Rear yard only, so not a side yard either.

district_yards_bind_accessory.note: Accessory uses take the district yards 'except as otherwise specifically provided'. The ADU has its own 6 ft side and rear setbacks. Attached accessory structures meet principal yards (23-30(c)(2)(A)).

accessory_structure_max_height_ft.note: Other accessory structures: 15 ft and one story.

accessory_cap_binds_adu.note: 'fifteen feet, with a maximum of one story, except for Accessory Dwelling Units as set forth below.'

owner_occupancy.note: No owner-occupancy rule. The ADU stays in single ownership with the parcel (23-30(c)(2)(B)(viii)).

max_adus.note: 'There shall not be more than one accessory dwelling unit created on any single parcel.' The code does not say whether a lot may have both an accessory apartment and an ADU.

short_term_rental_banned.note: Short-term rental is an allowable accessory use in every Table 17 district, 'Subject to compliance with Kennett Square Borough Code chapter 8, article VII.' Chapter 8 was not read. A 2026 ordinance (about August 17, 2026, not read) reportedly limits future short-term rentals to accessory units, owner occupied, capped at 20.

sale_apart_allowed.note: 'An accessory dwelling unit shall not be subdivided from the principal parcel, and shall remain under single ownership.'

spaces_required.note: 'Short-Term Rental; Accessory Apartment; Accessory Dwelling Unit | 1 Space per Bedroom (Maximum of 2 spaces per Dwelling Unit)'.

reading.value: One space per bedroom, at most two. An ADU has at most two bedrooms, so one or two spaces, plus two for the house (Table 7.1 A.1).

total_on_site.note: House 2 plus 1 or 2 for the unit, 3 or 4 in all. 23-65 also allows public parking and fee-in-lieu options in commercial districts.

max_building_coverage.note: By district: R-1 25%, R-2 30%, R-3 40%, R-3/PAO 40%, C-2 residential as R-3.

max_impervious.note: By district: R-1 35%, R-2 40%, R-3 60%, R-3/PAO 60%, C-2 residential as R-3.
